classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that two semicircular ends form one circle, identify its diameter from the separation of the straights, and add the straight lengths.

content.prompt: An athletics track is made up of two parallel straight sections that are 102 metres long and 62 metres apart, with two semicircular ends. Calculate the approximate distance travelled by an athlete who runs one lap of this track. Use $\pi\approx\dfrac{22}{7}$.

answer.worked:
The two semicircular ends form one circle of diameter $62\text{ m}$.

$$\begin{align*}P&=2\times102+\pi\times62\\P&\approx204+\frac{22}{7}\times62\\P&\approx204+\frac{1364}{7}\\P&\approx398\frac{6}{7}\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
